affo.title: AFFO
affo.content:
AFFO (adjusted funds from operations) is a property owner's distributable cash: net income excluding revaluations, adjusted for maintenance capex and lease incentives.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the valuation capitalises AFFO at the cost of equity; statutory net income is dominated by revaluation noise.

What to watch:

  • AFFO per share growth
  • Payout ratio (DPS / AFFO per share)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

npi.title: Net property income
npi.content:
Net property income (NPI) is gross rental income less direct property operating expenses -- the REIT-specific line between revenue and AFFO, before interest, tax and management fees.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the base-case DCF projects NPI forward directly (not revenue less a modelled margin), so this chart is the growth path the valuation is anchored to.

What to watch:

  • NPI growth versus the portfolio's contracted rent reviews (fixed uplifts, CPI-linked, market)
  • NPI margin (NPI / gross property income) for leakage into opex

dpu.title: Distribution per unit
dpu.content:
Distribution per unit (DPU) is the cash paid out per unit each year, in cents. It is set by the manager relative to AFFO per unit, not by statutory (revaluation-affected) earnings.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: DPU has been held flat at 9.75 cpu since FY2024 while AFFO per unit has kept growing -- the payout ratio is falling, which is conservative but also means unitholders are not yet seeing the full benefit of NPI growth in cash returned.

What to watch:

  • DPU growth resuming once the payout ratio normalises
  • DPU against AFFO per unit (payout ratio) rather than DPU alone

nta.title: Net tangible assets per unit
nta.content:
NTA per unit is net assets (predominantly the independently revalued property portfolio) divided by units on issue -- the REIT's book-value-per-share equivalent, and the anchor for the DCF's exit-multiple (P/NTA) cross-check.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: NTA per unit has fallen every year since the FY2022 cap-rate peak ($3.34 to $2.41 by FY2026) as valuers pushed capitalisation rates out; it is a mark-to-market of the property book, not an operating metric, so a falling NTA alongside rising NPI signals cap-rate expansion rather than a weaker portfolio.

What to watch:

  • NTA stabilising once cap rates plateau
  • Unit price against NTA (premium or discount to book)

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Vital Healthcare Property Trust: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
